title: Top 8 Best Phone Under 40000 in Bangladesh 2026
summary: Rising import duties and a weaker taka have pushed phone prices up in 2026, but great options still exist. We compare 8 top phone under 40000 in Bangladesh, from big batteries to sharp cameras.
intro: Confused about the best phone under 40000 in Bangladesh? Here are our top 8 picks for 2026.
html:
Over the last couple of months, mobile phone prices in Bangladesh have been rising. This is due to the global memory chip shortage, rising import duties from 2% to 4%, and a weaker taka against the dollar. In 2026, having a good smartphone is essential for everyone, whether you are a student, a working professional, or a homemaker. A mobile phone connects you to people and everything, which is important for almost every task you do daily, from important calls to social media browsing, daily photography to gaming. In our Bangladeshi phone market, people love to buy a feature-packed phone at a budget price.

That's where the budget and mid-range phone segments come in. The BDT 30,000 to 40,000 range has become the real battleground, the budget where most Bangladeshi buyers actually shop. 

But there's a problem. Every popular brand, including Xiaomi, Samsung, Oppo, Vivo, Tecno, Infinix, and more, is fighting for this price range. They launch new phones almost every month. More choices sound good, but they make picking the best one harder. You end up checking spec after spec, not knowing which phone truly fits your needs and budget. Here at Star Tech, a trusted mobile phone shop, we shortlisted the top 8 phone under 40000 in Bangladesh right now. Check below and pick the best mobile for you.

Before we get into the details, let’s take a quick side-by-side look at all 8 phones. Here, the table shows the display size, chipset, camera setup, battery, and key points so you can shortlist your favorites before reading the full breakdown below.

Samsung Galaxy A17 5G

Samsung's Galaxy A Series has long been a trusted name in Bangladesh. The Galaxy A17 5G continues that name with 6 major Android OS upgrades and 6 years of security patches, one of the longest software update commitments in this mid-range price segment. The Samsung phone delivers a 6.7‑inch Super AMOLED display that peaks at 800 nits, so you read the screen clearly even under direct sunlight. Corning Gorilla Glass Victus protects the panel, adding durability for daily use.

Samsung powers the device with the Exynos 1330 chipset and integrates Gemini AI tools like Gemini Live and Circle to Search. You rarely see these features under 40,000, and they handle everyday apps, social media, streaming, multitasking, and casual gaming smoothly. 

On the back, Samsung equips the Galaxy A17 5G with a 50MP main camera, a 5MP ultrawide lens, and a 2MP macro lens. You capture landscapes, close‑ups, and detailed shots with ease. Samsung also brings 5G connectivity to this price point, making the phone future‑ready. A 5000 mAh battery with 25W fast charging keeps the device running all day without worry.

Pros

  • 6 OS upgrades and 6 years of security updates.

  • Super AMOLED display and 5G connectivity.

Cons

  • Battery capacity is lower than some alternatives.

  • Exynos 1330 struggles with heavier games at high settings.

Who Should Buy the Samsung Galaxy A17 5G?

The Galaxy A17 5G is best for Samsung fans, students, homemakers, everyday users, casual gamers, and anyone who wants 5G connectivity with a quality AMOLED display.

HONOR X8d

The HONOR X8d uses a 7000 mAh battery with 45W fast charging, one of the largest in this best phone under 40,000 list. It easily lasts a full day on a single charge. The 6.77‑inch AMOLED display peaks at 3000 nits, making it one of the brightest panels here, so you read the screen clearly even under harsh midday sun.

The Honor phone runs on a Snapdragon 6s 4G Gen 2, handling messaging, social apps, video streaming, and regular multitasking smoothly. While HONOR doesn’t position it as a performance gaming phone, it still handles casual gaming without issue.

A 108MP main camera gives you high‑resolution shots for everyday photography. HONOR adds an under‑display fingerprint sensor and an IP65 rating, protecting the phone against dust and light rain, which is useful for Bangladesh’s unpredictable weather.

Pros

  • Bright 120Hz AMOLED display.

  • Large 7000 mAh battery.

Cons

  • No 5G connectivity.

  • Snapdragon 6s Gen 2 is an entry-level chipset.

Who Should Buy the HONOR X8d?

The HONOR X8d suits delivery riders, field sales staff, outdoor workers, mobile photographers, casual gamers, and anyone who spends a lot of time outdoors.

OPPO A6s Pro

Do you want the best selfie phone under 40,000 taka? The OPPO A6s Pro delivers with a 50MP front camera, giving sharper portraits, clearer video calls, and better social media shots even in dim light. Its 6.57‑inch FHD+ AMOLED display runs at 120Hz and reaches 1400 nits, so visuals stay smooth and bright outdoors.

OPPO powers the phone with MediaTek’s Helio G100 Max chipset and AI Game Boost, keeping gaming responsive even on weak networks. The Oppo phone suits everyday use for social media, messaging, streaming, photography, and multitasking while also handling casual gaming.

Durability sets this model apart. The IP69K rating protects against dust and high‑pressure water, making it ideal for rough environments. A 7000 mAh battery with 80W SuperVOOC charging recharges faster than most competitors, giving you all‑day power with quick top‑ups.

Pros

  • 50MP selfie camera and 80W fast charging.

  • IP69K dust and water-resistant rating.

Cons

  • Smaller 6.57" display compared to the 6.7"+ display.

  • No 5G connectivity.

Who Should Buy the OPPO A6s Pro?

The OPPO A6s Pro is best for buyers who prioritize durability, frequent selfie-takers and social media users, and anyone who wants the fastest possible charging on this list.

Tecno Pova Curve 2

Tecno targets gamers and power users with the Pova Curve 2. The phone packs a 6.78‑inch curved AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate, giving you smooth scrolling and gaming visuals. The display also uses a high‑frequency PWM system controls brightness, keeping the screen comfortable for long use.

The Dimensity 7100 5G is a 6 nm chipset with dedicated graphics performance. It offers a stronger platform for gaming and demanding apps than basic entry-level processors. The Tecno Pova Curve 2's 8000 mAh battery is another major attraction. It can suit heavy users who regularly spend long periods gaming, streaming, browsing, or using mobile data.

This Tecno phone also adds some extras for regular usability, like an under‑display fingerprint sensor, IP64 protection, dual speakers, and Dolby Atmos support. These features make the Tecno Pova Curve 2 more focused on entertainment and extended daily use.

Pros

  • 144Hz curved AMOLED display.

  • 8000mAh battery with 5G connectivity.

Cons

  • Camera setup is less versatile than some competitors.

  • IP64 rating offers basic splash resistance, not full water protection.

Who Should Buy the Tecno Pova Curve 2?

The Tecno Pova Curve 2 is best for mobile gamers, heavy phone users, and anyone who wants the smoothest AMOLED display and the biggest battery under 40000.

Vivo Y500

The Vivo Y500 is built for buyers who want the biggest screen and battery in one phone under a 40000 budget. Its 6.83-inch AMOLED display is the largest among the 8 best phone and supports a 120Hz refresh rate and HDR, making it ideal for video streaming, browsing, and everyday entertainment. At 8100 mAh, this Y500 has the largest battery capacity on the list, built for genuine multi-day light use. The Unisoc T7300 processor handles everyday tasks and moderate workloads. The Vivo phone also has a 32MP front camera, which gives selfie and video-call users a higher-resolution option. Durability is another important part of the Y500. Its dual IP68 and IP69 ratings provide stronger protection against dust and water than phones without an official IP rating.

Pros

  • Very large 8100 mAh battery.

  • IP68/IP69 protection against dust and water.

Cons

  • No 5G connectivity.

  • Performance is not designed for high-end gaming.

Who Should Buy the Vivo Y500?

The Vivo Y500 is best for heavy video watchers, travelers, students, and buyers in humid or rainy environments who want maximum battery and screen size.

Redmi Note 15 5G

Xiaomi builds the Redmi Note 15 5G to feel complete instead of chasing one standout feature, and that balance shows in daily use. I like how the 108MP main camera captures sharper detail than the 50MP sensors most competitors use at this price point; it’s easily one of the strongest cameras on this best phone list.

This Xiaomi phone pairs with the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 chipset, built on a 4 nm process. It gives you smooth multitasking, social media, and casual gaming while keeping power draw efficient. The 6.77‑inch FHD+ AMOLED curved display runs at 120Hz, so scrolling feels smoother and colors look rich, even compared to pricier phones.

What really stands out to me is the dual IP65 and IP66 certification. It protects against dust and low‑pressure water jets, a detail many competitors skip. The 20MP front camera also produces brighter, more natural selfies than the typical 13MP shooters in this mobile phone price segment.

Xiaomi adds practical touches like a 5520 mAh silicon‑carbon battery with 45W Turbo Charging, expandable storage, NFC, and an in‑display fingerprint sensor. Together, these features make the Redmi Note 15 5G one of the most well-rounded phone under 40,000.

Pros

  • 4 nm Snapdragon chipset with 5G.

  • 108MP main camera and 120Hz AMOLED display.

Cons

  • Battery capacity is lower than several competitors.

  • Charging speed is not the fastest in this group.

Who Should Buy the Redmi Note 15 5G?

The Redmi Note 15 5G is best for students, professionals, casual gamers, homemakers, and anyone who wants dependable, well-rounded performance without a single glaring weakness.

Infinix Note Edge

The Infinix Note Edge brings a curved 1.5K AMOLED display to the best phone list. Its 6.78-inch screen uses a 120Hz refresh rate, giving the phone a smooth visual experience for scrolling and supported games. The curved display also gives it a more flagship feel. Eye-care features and high-frequency PWM dimming can help people who spend long periods looking at the screen. 

The Dimensity 7100 is a 6 nm 5G chipset with capable graphics and handles everyday multitasking, social media, streaming, photography, and gaming with ease. The 6500 mAh battery further strengthens the Infinix Note Edge phone's appeal for heavy users. Its 45W charging support helps bring the large battery back to a useful charge level faster. The Infinix phone also includes an in-display fingerprint sensor, IP65 protection, and dual speakers tuned with JBL.

Pros

  • 1.5K curved AMOLED display with 120 Hz refresh rate.

  • Large 6500mAh battery with 5G support.

Cons

  • Camera setup is relatively simple.

  • Front camera resolution is lower than some competitors.

Who Should Buy the Infinix Note Edge?

The Infinix Note Edge suits style-conscious buyers, younger users, and anyone who watches a lot of video and wants the sharpest screen for the money.

Tecno Camon 50

Tecno positions the Camon series as its camera‑first lineup, and the Camon 50 keeps that promise. The 32MP front camera captures sharper, more detailed selfies than most competitors at this price range, making it a strong choice for social media and video calls.

The Tecno phone uses a 6.78‑inch AMOLED panel with 1.5K resolution and a 144 Hz refresh rate, so you enjoy smooth visuals whether you’re gaming or just scrolling. The Helio G200 Ultimate processor runs everyday apps, multitasking, social media, streaming, and moderate gaming without slowing down.

Tecno gives you up to 256 GB of storage and plenty of space for photos, videos, and apps. On the back, the 50MP main camera with a large 1/1.56‑inch sensor and OIS works alongside an 8MP ultrawide lens, giving you versatile shooting options.

A 6500 mAh battery with 45W Super Charge keeps the Tecno Camon 50 powered through long days. Tecno also adds an in‑display fingerprint sensor, dual speakers with Dolby Atmos, NFC, and Type‑C connectivity, making the Camon 50 practical for both entertainment and daily use.

Pros

  • 50MP OIS camera with a large main sensor.

  • 1.5K 144Hz AMOLED display and 6500mAh battery.

Cons

  • No 5G connectivity.

  • Performance is less focused on high-end gaming.

Who Should Buy the Tecno Camon 50?

Let’s find out. The Tecno Camon 50 is best for content creators, social media regulars, and anyone who takes more photos of themselves than of anything else.

Which Phone Under 40000 Fits Your Needs?

Picking the best phone under 40000 comes down to what you actually use your phone for. If battery life matters most, the Vivo Y500 and Tecno Pova Curve 2 5G lead with 8000 mAh-plus capacities. If you want the smoothest display experience, the Infinix Note Edge's 1.5K curved AMOLED panel is hard to beat at this price. Photography-focused buyers should look at the Redmi Note 15 5G for its 108MP main camera or the Tecno Camon 50 and OPPO A6s Pro for standout selfie cameras. If long-term software support and a trusted brand matter more than raw specs, the Samsung Galaxy A17 5G remains a safe, dependable choice. No matter which of the best phone under 40000 you're considering from this list, check out Star Tech for competitive prices and availability.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQS)

Question-1:

Which phone under 40000 has the best camera?

The Redmi Note 15 5G stands out with its 108MP main sensor, while the Tecno Camon 50 and OPPO A6s Pro shine for selfies.

Question-2:

Which phone under 40000 is best for gaming?

The Tecno Pova Curve 2 with its Dimensity 7100 5G chipset and 144Hz AMOLED display is built for gamers. The Infinix Note Edge also offers smooth visuals and JBL‑tuned speakers.

Question-3:

Which phone under 40000 has the longest battery life?

The Vivo Y500 (8100 mAh) and Tecno Pova Curve 2 (8000 mAh) lead the pack, lasting well beyond a full day.

Question-4:

Which phone under 40000 offers the best durability?

The OPPO A6s Pro with its IP69K rating provides the strongest dust and water resistance.

Question-5:

Which phone under 40000 gets the longest software updates?

The Samsung Galaxy A17 5G promises 6 OS upgrades and 6 years of security patches, giving unmatched long‑term value.
